name: MathlibAnnex.Satellite.exists_goodSatellitePackage
title: A finite absolute-maximizing family almost norms the unit sphere

content.display_title: A finite absolute-maximizing family almost norms the unit sphere
content.one_sentence_role: Chooses the inverse bound, net and weight before fixing one satellite family.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and use reference coordinates $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the sup norm. Let $p:V\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in V).$$
Thus $p$ is a norm. We use $p$ for the model distance and $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ for reference-coordinate estimates; the two norms are allowed to coincide. A $p$-dual contraction is a continuous real linear functional $r$ satisfying $|r(x)|\le p(x)$ for every $x$. Let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be the standard coordinate vectors. For an ordered family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ of continuous real linear functionals on $V$, put
$$M_F=(\ell_i(e_j))_{i,j},\quad T_Fx=(\ell_i(x))_i=M_Fx,\quad
\mathcal U_p=\{F:\forall i,x,\ |\ell_i(x)|\le p(x)\}.$$
For a real number $\eta$, define the attained maximum and near-maximal set by
$$D_p=\max_{F\in\mathcal U_p}|\det M_F|>0,\qquad
\mathcal N_{p,\eta}=\{F\in\mathcal U_p:D_p-\eta\le|\det M_F|\}.$$
Admissibility is measured with $p$; the matrices are written in the fixed reference coordinates. Suppose $0<\eta<D_p$ and $\varepsilon>0$. The conclusion chooses a number $K>0$ with the uniform bound
$$p(M_F^{-1}v)\le K\|v\|_\infty\qquad(F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta},\ v\in V),$$
then a finite center set $C$ and a weight $w>0$. More precisely, put
$$\rho=\frac{\min(\varepsilon,1)}{8K}>0,\qquad
\mathcal A_K=\{c\in V:1/K\le\|c\|_\infty\le1\},$$
$$C\subseteq\mathcal A_K,\qquad \forall c\in\mathcal A_K,\quad\exists a\in C,\quad\|c-a\|_\infty\le\rho.$$
Index the coefficients by $a\in C$ and put $c_a=a$. For a functional $r$, let $M_F[i\leftarrow r]$ replace row $i$ by $(r(e_j))_j$. A configuration $Q=(F,s)$ consists of a base frame and a family of additional continuous real linear functionals $s_a$, called satellites. Its polynomial, admissible set and coefficient budget are
$$\Phi_{w,c}(F,s)=w\det M_F+\sum_{a\in C}\sum_i(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a],$$
$$\Omega_p^C=\{(F,s):F\in\mathcal U_p,\ \forall a\in C,x\in V,\ |s_a(x)|\le p(x)\}.$$
$$S_p(c)=D_p\sum_{a\in C}\sum_{i=1}^n |(c_a)_i|.$$
For the selected absolute maximizer $Q=(F,s)\in\Omega_p^C$, that is,
$$|\Phi_{w,c}(Q^\prime)|\le |\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|\qquad(Q'\in\Omega_p^C),$$
the same choices satisfy $S_p(c)<w\eta$ and
$$\forall x\in V\ (p(x)=1),\quad\exists a\in C,\quad 1-\varepsilon<|s_a(x)|.$$
content.assumptions: The real norm model with its comparison constants, $\eta>0$, $\eta<D_p$ and $\varepsilon>0$ are the only assumptions. Neither $n>0$, $\varepsilon<1$, a nonempty sphere nor nonempty centers are assumed. The number $K$, its uniform bound, the finite net, and the weight are outputs, not further assumptions.
content.conclusion: One finite family, obtained from the selected absolute-maximizing configuration after fixing the net and weight, works for every unit vector. The center/index may depend on the unit vector. Positivity of the weight and its strict budget inequality are also outputs.
content.proof_summary: Fix a uniform inverse bound, choose a finite coefficient net, choose a dominating weight, maximize the absolute polynomial, and then detect each unit vector using that same family.

proof_steps.text: **Choose the common bound before the net.** Apply [existence of a common near-maximal inverse bound](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L620-L627) to the same space $V$ equipped with the norm $p$ and the standard basis and to $0\le\eta<D_p$. Its record supplies $K>0$ and $p(M_F^{-1}c)\le K\|c\|_\infty$ for every $F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta}$ and $c$. Set $\rho=\min(\varepsilon,1)/(8K)$; $\varepsilon>0$ and $K>0$ ensure $\rho>0$.

**Take a net in the reference coordinates.** The annulus $\mathcal A_K$ is closed and contained in the reference closed unit ball, so it is compact in finite-dimensional $V$. Apply [finite covering of a compact set](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Cover.lean#L122-L125) with this actual set and the nonzero radius $\rho$ (stored as a nonnegative real). Its outputs are a finite $C\subseteq\mathcal A_K$ covering every point of $\mathcal A_K$ to reference distance at most $\rho$. The [finite coefficient-net record](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L255-L259) stores exactly its centers, their containment, their finiteness and this cover property. Each $a\in C$ is used as the coefficient vector $c_a=a$; no maximizer or unit vector has yet been chosen.

**Turn this net into detection uniformly over near-maximal frames.** For every $F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta}$ and $p(x)=1$, contraction and reconstruction give
   $$\|T_Fx\|_\infty\le1,\qquad 1=p(x)=p(M_F^{-1}T_Fx)\le K\|T_Fx\|_\infty.$$
   Thus $T_Fx\in\mathcal A_K$. Choose $a\in C$ with $\|T_Fx-a\|_\infty\le\rho$. The same inverse estimate gives
   $$p(x-M_F^{-1}a)=p(M_F^{-1}(T_Fx-a))\le K\|T_Fx-a\|_\infty\le K\rho.$$
   These are the inputs and output of [coefficient detection supplied by this net](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L1035-L1042); detection holds for every near-maximal frame, before the selected maximizer is known.

**Choose the weight and then the configuration.** With the already fixed finite coefficient family, set $w=S_p(c)/\eta+1$. Nonnegativity of the budget and $\eta>0$ give $w>0$ and $S_p(c)<w\eta$. The product $\Omega_p^C$ is compact and nonempty: its dual contraction rows are closed, bounded by $b_p$ in reference operator norm, and finite in number; zero rows are admissible. The continuous function $|\Phi_{w,c}|$ therefore attains its maximum. Fix the selected $Q=(F,s)$ once. Apply [absolute maximization giving a near-maximal base](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L713-L732) with this positive weight, strict budget inequality, admissibility and absolute maximum. It gives $F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta}$.

**Apply detection to the same satellites and retain strictness.** For arbitrary $p(x)=1$, apply [the almost-norming satellite estimate](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L993-L1012) with exactly the fixed $K,\rho,c,Q$, the gap, the detection already proved, and the base membership just obtained. It gives an $a$ from this same family with
   $$|s_a(x)|\ge1-2K\rho=1-\frac{\min(\varepsilon,1)}4>1-\varepsilon.$$
   Indeed $0<\min(\varepsilon,1)\le\varepsilon$ implies $\min(\varepsilon,1)/4\le\varepsilon/4<\varepsilon$. Thus the error is strictly less than $\varepsilon$, without assuming $\varepsilon<1$. For $n=0$ the unit sphere is empty, the annulus and centers may be empty, and the final universal statement is vacuous.

content.lean_realization_notes:
A common inverse bound consists of a number $K>0$ and the uniform estimate
$$p(M_F^{-1}c)\le K\|c\|_\infty\qquad(F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta},\ c\in V).$$
It is fixed independently of the particular frame and coefficient. When $\eta<D_p$, every such frame has nonzero determinant. The annulus itself is [the coefficient annulus](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L229-L230). The [strict epsilon version](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L1015-L1032), [finite-net absolute-maximizer conclusion](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L1045-L1066) and [weight choice for a given net](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L1094-L1112) preserve this order of choices. As a contextual connection, define $A_Qx=((\ell_i(x))_i,(s_a(x))_a)$ with the sup norm on its finite coordinates. [the upper bound for that coordinate map](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteSup.lean#L382-L392) uses admissibility to give $\|A_Qx\|_\infty\le p(x)$, while [one satellite coordinate bounds the whole map from below](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteSup.lean#L394-L402) gives $1-\varepsilon<\|A_Qx\|_\infty$ on the unit sphere. For $x\ne0$, apply the latter to $x/p(x)$ and use linearity to get $(1-\varepsilon)p(x)<\|A_Qx\|_\infty$, as in [the lower bound for every nonzero vector](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteSup.lean#L420-L459). This only explains the assigned coordinate-map context; no later classification is asserted.
